analysis.title: ETP Flow Update: EMEA UCITS ETP flows, 26 October 2026
key_insights: EMEA UCITS ETPs took in $10.2B net last week (15-21 Oct 2026) vs $8.6B the week prior. Equity, fixed income and commodity flows were all positive.
Equity ETPs attracted $5.9B, down from $6.2B. Fixed income inflows rose to $3.5B from $2.9B. Commodities rose to $794m from $47m.
Developed market equities took $5.5B, down from $6.0B. Global DM strategies took $3.9B, little changed. Europe inflows rose to $1.1B from $75m, while North America fell to $517m from $1.8B.
US single-country equity inflows fell to $562m from $1.8B. Japan took $169m and Switzerland $168m. Canada had the largest outflows at -$65m.
Within US size exposures, Large Caps took $496m (vs $1.9B previously), Small Caps had outflows of -$118m and Mid Caps took $3m.
Emerging market equity ETPs took $320m, up from $177m. South Korea took $340m (vs $58m) while China had outflows of -$411m (vs -$339m).
Active equity ETPs took $665m, down from $967m. Alpha-Seeking took $504m, Outcome $129m, and Exposure had outflows of -$2m.
Sustainable equity ETPs returned to inflows of $58m after -$337m. Europe took $207m and APAC $169m, while North America had outflows of -$402m (vs -$531m).
Sector ETPs had outflows of -$49m, an improvement from -$541m. Energy took $149m, Health Care $141m and Technology $103m. Financials had outflows of -$373m (vs -$911m).
Thematic ETPs took $136m, down from $247m. Robotics & AI took $161m, and the AI sub-theme took $131m and Cybersecurity $72m. Climate Energy had outflows of -$141m and Clean Energy -$144m.
Factor flows shifted to Quality ($329m, vs $78m) and Low Volatility ($216m, vs $8m). Value reversed to outflows of -$291m from +$22m.
Income strategies took $349m, Factors $324m and Alternatives $159m (vs -$30m).
Commodity ETPs took $794m. Gold took $704m (vs $165m), Oil $81m (vs -$102m) and Silver $62m (vs -$41m). Other Commodities had outflows of -$53m.
Fixed income ETPs took $3.5B, of which index strategies took $3.1B. Government bonds took $1.5B (vs $1.0B) while Investment Grade took $585m (vs $1.3B).
Within government bonds, USD exposures took $1.4B (vs $746m), EUR Government $59m (vs $224m) and GBP Government had outflows of -$62m.
Money Market took $337m (vs $51m) and High Yield $259m. EM debt returned to inflows of $73m after -$315m, with Local EM at $156m and Hard EM at -$83m.
Active fixed income ETPs took $449m, more than double $220m. High Yield took $179m within Alpha-Seeking, while Investment Grade had outflows of -$115m. Securitised took $209m within Exposure.
Indexed sustainable fixed income ETPs took $87m, down from $655m.
UCITS ETP dollar average daily volume was $23.5B (1.1x the 3-month average). Equity was $17.8B (1.2x), fixed income $5.0B (1.1x) and commodities $0.7B (0.7x).

sector_views.rationale: Energy ETPs led sector inflows at $149m last week, per the flow data. This describes flows, not a bank view.
Health Care ETPs took $141m, second among sectors. This describes flows, not a bank view.
Technology ETPs took $103m. Robotics & AI and AI sub-themes also drew inflows. This describes flows, not a bank view.
Financials had outflows of -$373m, the largest sector outflow, though selling eased from -$911m. This describes flows, not a bank view.

vol_and_positioning: Flow positioning: Quality ($329m) and Low Volatility ($216m) drew inflows while Value had outflows of -$291m, mainly Value-Global (-$234m) and Value-Europe (-$62m).
China-focused ETPs had outflows of -$411m, the second week of heavy selling after -$339m. South Korea took $340m.
UCITS ETP trading volumes ran 1.1x the 3-month average. Equity was 1.2x and commodities 0.7x.
